items.text: Limited to 20 minutes per night?. Warriors head coach Steve Kerr said Friday that Horford will likely be limited to 20 minutes per night this season, according to Warriors reporter Joseph Dycus. Golden State's starting lineup is likely to be fluid, but most nights it's likely to be Horford starting alongside Draymond Green. In addition to reduced workloads this season, Horford may also have a maintenance plan similar to his Boston days which included days off during back-to-back sets.

Knicks could make move. The Knicks could be open to signing Burks before the start of the 2025-26 season, according to James L. Edwards III of The Athletic. The Knicks have one roster spot open, but they can only fill it by signing a veteran player via a minimum deal, which limits their options. Even though Burks wouldn't add depth at point guard, which is an area New York desperately needs another option, he could be a valuable scoring weapon off the bench due to his three-point shooting. Burks spent the 2024-25 season as a member of the Heat but previously played for the Knicks in 2020-21, 2021-22 and 2023-24.

The Thunder elected to rest their main guys for the first two road games of the preseason, but Caruso isn't dealing with any sort of injury. His next opportunity to play will come in Oklahoma City's preseason home opener against Charlotte on Thursday.

Scouts not in love with him. Five talent evaluators from around the NBA were asked about Sarr, and none believe he'll be able to become the best or second-best scoring option on a contending team down the road, according to Josh Robbins of The Athletic. Sarr, who's recovering from a calf injury but might be ready for the start of the regular season in late October, averaged 13.0 points, 6.5 rebounds and 1.5 blocks over 67 regular-season games as a rookie in 2024-25. However, there are different concerns about the development of his game. One scout believes he needs to bulk up to be an effective rim protector, while another thinks his shot will never be good enough to play as a stretch big man.

Throws dart at Antetokounmpo. Sengun said that Antetokounmpo "isn't a great passer" after Turkey defeated Greece in the EuroBasket semifinals earlier this month. "He's not a great passer. He's an amazing player, you know, but he's not a great passer. So we just tried to help and jump to close the paint," Sengun said, per Edvinas Jablonskis of BasketNews.com. Even though the comments didn't escalate into an altercation between the two players, it's uncommon to see a star player criticizing another in such an open way. Antetokounmpo might not be the elite passer Sengun is, but the former is certainly a player capable of making things happen as a playmaker. Antetokounmpo averaged 6.5 assists per game in 2024-25 over 76 regular-season games and has dished out at least 5.5 dimes per game in each of his last seven seasons in the league.

Trade talks have stalled. Trade talks for Wiggins between the Heat and Lakers appear to have stalled due to a high asking price from Miami, Jovan Buha of The Athletic reports. "We're talking basically everything or close to everything that the Lakers could offer from a top-end asset standpoint," Buha said. "So I don't think that is going to happen. I don't think the Lakers are trading Rui Hachimura, a first, and Dalton Knecht for Andrew Wiggins. That's not fair value. That's not a realistic trade. I think Miami's playing hardball. We'll see if they soften their stance." It's clear that the Heat rate Wiggins highly, as he's a capable two-way wing still in the midst of his prime. During the 2024-25 regular season, Wiggins put up averages of 18.0 points, 4.5 rebounds, 2.6 assists, 0.8 blocks and 1.0 steals in 30.7 minutes per contest.

Will operate as primary playmaker. Davis is expected to operate as the Mavericks' primary playmaker in the early stages of the 2025-26 season, according to Grant Afseth of Dallas Hoops Journal. Davis' new role is an implementation by Jay Triano, the Mavericks' top offensive assistant coach for this season. He used Domantas Sabonis as Sacramento's primary playmaker during his time with the Kings, and Davis figures to have the same role in Dallas, especially with Kyrie Irving sidelined due to a knee injury. Davis averaged 4.4 assists per game in the 2024-25 regular-season campaign.

In midst of strong offseason. Edwards' business manager Justin Holland said the guard has "completely bought in" to his offseason regimen, Chris Hine of the Minneapolis Star Tribune reports. "He heard the noise," Holland said of the criticism Edwards received at times in the postseason. "Every summer we'll attack the offseason better than the year before and he's proven he takes his work ethic a lot more seriously from year to year." Holland added that he sees "a different look in his eye." As for what Edwards is specifically working on, Holland played that close to his chest and indicated that Edwards wants to keep that quiet.

Set for more ball-handling duties. Thompson is expected to have a bigger role as a ball-handling presence in 2025-26, according to Hunter Patterson of The Athletic. Thompson's ball-in-hand role last season was mostly limited to fastbreaks and dunks, but the Pistons have been experimenting with a bigger role in playmaking for the third-year forward. Thompson's ability to change speeds and use his above-average strength and athleticism to get to the rim could be a reason why the Pistons are looking to expand Thompson's ball-handling role. That said, Cade Cunningham should continue to be the Pistons' primary offense initiator once the regular season begins.

Reaves didn't play in Los Angeles' last preseason game, Oct. 5, for undisclosed reasons, though it was likely just a maintenance day for the veteran. Including Sunday's game, the Lakers will have four more exhibitions ahead of Opening Night.

Finishing up strong offseason. Head coach JJ Redick stated Thursday that Reaves has looked like the best player on the court anytime he's been in the gym this summer, Mike Trudell of Spectrum SportsNet reports. Not only is Reaves playing at a high level during offseason workouts, but Redick also pointed out that the shooting guard is in excellent shape. "He's really strong. His burst, his athleticism," said Redick. "It's evident that he spent a lot of time working on his body this summer." The upcoming season is shaping up to be an important campaign for Reaves, who is eyeing a contract extension following the completion of his fifth year in the NBA.

Not worried about future. Dosunmu said Friday that he's not thinking about his future with the franchise, Joe Cowley of the Chicago Sun Times reports. "My main focus is just taking it one day at a time, not worrying about next July or whenever it is, because that's going to happen when it's going to happen," Dosunmu said. "Just stay in the moment." Dosunmu is entering the final season of his contract and is set to enter unrestricted free agency next summer, and there's no guarantee the Bulls will keep him with Coby White set to hit unrestricted free agency at the same time. Naturally, Dosunmu is likely going to see his name in the rumor mill quite a bit as a result.

Won't play Tuesday. Sheppard (undisclosed) won't play in Tuesday's preseason game against the Timberwolves, Tony East of WTHR Channel 13 Indianapolis reports. It's not immediately clear what type of injury Sheppard is dealing with. However, coach Rick Carlisle expects him to return at some point during the preseason. Sheppard's next chance to play comes Saturday against the Thunder.

Injury not serious. Adebayo's knee injury that he picked up in Monday's preseason loss to Atlanta is not serious, Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald reports. Jackson reports that Adebayo's injury is just a contusion, but it remains to be seen if he will play in the preseason finale Friday. For now, there doesn't seem to be any indication that his status for Opening Night will be in danger. Overall, Adebayo had a tough showing in four exhibitions, as he shot 27.6 percent from the field.

Linked to New York. Simmons could be in consideration for New York's 14th roster spot, Stefan Bondy of the New York Post reports. Bondy adds that he's heard conflicting reports as to whether or not the interest in Simmons is genuine. According to Bondy, Malcolm Brogdon and Landry Shamet are also in consideration for the 14th spot. Due to his injury history and lack of consistency, it's hard to imagine Simmons getting anything more than a deal for the veteran's minimum.

Re-evaluated in three weeks. Wizards general manager Will Dawkins said Wednesday that Coulibaly (thumb) will be re-evaluated in a few weeks, Chase Hughes of Monumental Sports Network reports. Dawkins said that based on Coulibaly's timetable, he's likely to miss all of training camp and return around the first or second week of the season. Coulibaly underwent surgery Sept. 12 to repair a ligament tear in his right thumb, but prospective fantasy managers will be relieved to hear that he's not facing an extended absence.

Back in action during EuroBasket. Coulibaly (hamstring) logged 10 points in 22 minutes of action for France during Sunday's 92-77 win over Greece in EuroBasket exhibition play, per Giorgos Kyriakidis of BasketNews.com. Subscribe now to instantly reveal our take on this news.

Recovery timeline updated. Coulibaly, who underwent surgery to repair a torn ligament in his right thumb Sept. 12, is expected to miss six to eight weeks, according to Grant Afseth of RG reports. This means Coulibaly will likely be sidelined for at least the first week of the season, which tips off Oct. 21. Afseth notes that even if Coulibaly were to get back to full health on the earlier side of that timeline, he would still have to get his conditioning back up to par. "Usually, you're not touching a basketball, unless it's just to do off-hand work, until that six-week mark," a source told Afseth. "Then he'd have to do contact work before playing." This news could see Coulibaly's fantasy draft stock take a hit, but he remains an intriguing late-round pick after averaging 12.3 points, 5.0 rebounds, 3.4 assists and 1.3 steals during the 2024-25 regular season.

Likely to work as third option. Beal is expected to operate as the third scoring option for the Clippers in the 2025-26 season, according to Duane Rankin of AZCentral.com. Beal, who will be playing alongside Kawhi Leonard and James Harden, will likely be a third option for the Clippers, according to head coach Tyronn Lue. However, a bigger role in case either of the other two stars is absent or resting isn't out of the question based on Lue's recent comments. "He's definitely going to be big help for us offensively," Lue said. "We're going to need him to score, but outside of scoring, we're going to need him to make plays for other guys." Beal spent the 2024-25 season with the Suns and averaged 17.0 points per game, his lowest mark since his rookie year, across 53 regular-season appearances.

Peterson has high expectations. Hornets executive vice president of basketball operations Jeff Peterson raved about Miller's potential at Media Day on Monday, Langston Wertz of The Charlotte Observer reports. "I don't want to put a cap or a ceiling on him," Peterson said, "because Brandon can be as good as he wants to be. He can be a Hall of Famer. And he knows the expectations on him this season. More importantly, he has those same expectations for himself." Miller averaged 21.0 points, 4.9 rebounds, 3.6 assists and 1.1 steals per game in his 27 regular-season appearances in 2024-25 before undergoing a season-ending wrist surgery in late January, but the forward is healthy entering the preseason and could be poised to make a major leap in his third campaign.

Comfortable in playmaking role. Ingram looked comfortable as a playmaker and offense orchestrator in the Raptors' preseason opener against the Nuggets on Monday, according to Michael Grange of Sportsnet.ca. Grange noted that the veteran forward looked "perfectly comfortable" generating half-court offense, and that was one of the reasons why Toronto traded for him before the deadline in the 2024-25 campaign. Ingram had a team-high 19 points while making six of his 12 shots from the floor in Monday's loss to the Nuggets. If he stays healthy, Ingram should be one of the Raptors' primary offensive weapons once the 2025-26 regular season begins.

Murray talks him up. At Media Day on Monday, Jamal Murray really talked up Johnson's offensive ability, Ryan Blackburn of MileHighSports.com reports. "He's all-around. He can shoot, he can dribble a bit better than I thought he could," Murray said. "I think he'll be our leading scorer a lot of nights." Johnson's fit in Denver is certainly exciting, as he'll be supplied a ton of open looks by arguably the best passer in the NBA in Nikola Jokic. Johnson is a career 39.2 percent shooter from beyond the arc and is coming off a campaign in Brooklyn in which he averaged a career-high 18.8 points per game during the regular season.

Busy at free-throw line Sunday. Thomas scored a team-high 16 points (4-12 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 8-10 FT) while adding four rebounds, an assist and a block in 26 minutes during Sunday's 111-109 preseason win over the Suns in Macao. The fifth-year guard continues to put together a productive exhibition schedule as one of the focal points of the Nets' offense along with Michael Porter. Thomas will be an unrestricted free agent next offseason, so he has extra motivation to improve on the career-best 24.0 points, 3.8 assists, 3.3 boards and 2.7 threes he averaged in 2024-25, albeit in only 25 regular-season games.

Marks addresses his future. Nets general manager Sean Marks said Thomas' decision to take the qualifying offer doesn't mean he won't be with the team for the future, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports. "He's approached this in a very mature manner," Marks said. "It's part of the business, maybe the ugly part of the business, when you can't find a common ground... He's a Net. He knows that. He's been very upfront, very mature... I think both sides understand what's at stake, but I also don't want to jump to conclusions. Just because a common ground couldn't be met this summer doesn't mean he's not a Net in the future or throughout this season." After a drama-filled offseason, these statements from Marks are at least a little reassuring for any prospective fantasy managers wanting to roll the dice on Thomas this season.

Strong season incoming?. Rylan Stiles of SI.com is expecting Wallace to make a leap in his third NBA season. Wallace shot 35.6 percent from beyond the arc in the 2024-25 regular season compared to 41.9 percent as a rookie, and Stiles is projecting some positive regression in that regard. Stiles notes that Wallace ranked in the 81st percentile as a cutter and put up 1.22 points per possession as a pick-and-roll man in guard-to-guard screening sets, so his shooting could be the final piece to the puzzle. Overall, the guard is coming off a regular season in which he averaged 8.4 points, 3.4 rebounds, 2.5 assists, 1.8 steals, 0.5 blocks and 1.1 three-pointers in 27.6 minutes per contest.

Agrees to deal with LAC. The Clippers agreed to a one-year deal with Paul on Monday, NBA reporter Chris Haynes reports. Paul will end his NBA career where he had arguably the most success, as he will join forces with Kawhi Leonard and James Harden for his farewell tour. The Wake Forest product spent six seasons with the Clippers before stints with the Rockets, Thunder, Suns, Warriors and Spurs. During the 2024-25 campaign with San Antonio, the veteran point guard played in all 82 regular-season games, averaging 8.8 points, 3.6 rebounds, 7.4 assists and 1.3 steals per game, shooting 42.7 percent from the floor and 37.7 percent from beyond the arc.

No friction with Harden. According to Law Murray of The Athletic, there is no lingering friction between Paul and James Harden. Paul and Harden have a history from their Houston days, but Murray reports that both players will be on the same page in Los Angeles. Clippers president of basketball operations Lawrence Frank has already declared that Paul will back up Harden next season, and noted that he's excited about the depth of the team. "I'll knock on wood, but the reality is for any NBA team, the amount of times you have your top 10 all available is usually 21 to 25 times throughout the course of a year," Frank said. "So, you literally need everyone on your roster to be able to contribute."

Agrees to deal with Celtics. Boucher (illness) has agreed to sign a one-year, $3.3 million contract with the Celtics, Shams Charania of ESPN reports. After spending the last seven years with the Raptors, Boucher will land with Boston to help shore up the team's new-look frontcourt. It's plausible that veteran big man will open the 2025-26 season in a starting role, considering Boston has left Al Horford unsigned in addition to trading away Kristaps Porzingis and Georges Niang this offseason. Over 50 regular-season contests last year, Boucher averaged 10.0 points, 4.5 rebounds, 0.7 assists and 1.4 three-pointers in 17.2 minutes per game.

To play key role in Boston. Boucher is expected to have a "significant role" in Boston's frontcourt, ESPN's Shams Charania reported Tuesday. Boucher agreed to a one-year, $3.3 million contract with the Celtics on Tuesday, giving them some much-needed depth up front -- the Celtics lost Kristaps Porzingis, Luke Kornet and Al Horford this offseason. This sets up an interesting training camp in Boston, as it's not out of the question that Boucher wins a starting job, with Sam Hauser and Neemias Queta currently penciled in as the starting four and five, respectively.

Could play in two-center lineups. In regards to the addition of Capela, Rockets general manager Rafael Stone said he anticipates using some two-center lineups in 2025-26, according to Rocket Fuel. "We loved that lineup once we discovered it last year. We thought it was really, really effective for us," Stone said. "Also, Clint just adds something we don't have in terms of being a center who can move a little bit easier on the perimeter, also as a lob threat. Finally, we just think depth is super important. As we're trying to make it through the season, we don't want there to be huge drop-offs. We did not anticipate going into free agency that we would be able to get Clint, but we were ecstatic when that materialized." Although Alperen Sengun is a cornerstone of the franchise, these comments from Stone seem to imply that Capela could be involved enough to have a fantasy impact with his new team. He averaged 21.4 minutes during the regular season with the Hawks in 2024-25 and nearly averaged a double-double with 8.9 points and 8.5 rebounds.

Along with Nikola Jokic, Jamal Murray and Aaron Gordon, Braun will sit out the Nuggets' preseason finale. His next opportunity to suit up will be in the team's regular-season opener against Golden State on Thursday.

Perfect from field in preseason win. Braun recorded 19 points (8-8 FG, 3-3 3Pt), two rebounds, two assists and two steals across 22 minutes in Monday's 112-108 preseason win over the Raptors. Subscribe now to instantly reveal our take on this news.

Wants to spend career with Nuggets. Braun wants to play with the Nuggets for his entire career, according to Mark Medina of Sportskeeda. "That has been my whole career. I have wanted to win in one spot," Braun said. "That's how I am as a person." Braun acknowledged that he has never switched teams in AAU, high school or college, and that he's not planning to leave Denver any time soon. "I want to win as a Nugget. I don't want to win anywhere else. Me winning as a Nugget means more than something somewhere else. Being grateful for the people here drives me to want to win in a Nuggets uniform," he added. Braun is eligible for a rookie-scale extension, and the deadline to sign a new contract is Oct. 20, only a few days before the start of the regular season.

Murray-Boyles produced 12 points (4-8 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 3-3 FT), seven rebounds, six assists and two blocks in 23 minutes in Wednesday's 130-122 preseason win over the Kings. Murray looked no worse for wear after appearing to roll his ankle during Monday's exhibition defeat to the Nuggets, chipping in across several areas Wednesday. The rookie first-rounder certainly benefited from the absence of Scottie Barnes (knee), and the former appears ticketed for a reserve role for Opening Night. That said, Murray-Boyles may not have as clear a path to minutes once Barnes is ready to get back into the fold for Toronto.

Expected to crack rotation. Michael Grange of Sportsnet reported Tuesday that Murray-Boyles is expected to crack Toronto's 10-man rotation. "It's a good bet that the Raptors will give every chance to recent lottery pick Collin Murray-Boyles to stick in the rotation, and the early returns are that he's going to be hard to move out of that spot," Grange said. Murray-Boyles, who was the No. 9 pick in the 2025 NBA Draft, has had a terrific training camp by all accounts. Minutes won't be easy to come by behind Scottie Barnes and Brandon Ingram, but Murray-Boyles' ability to defend multiple spots on the floor will certainly help his case.

Ready for training camp. Wizards general manager Will Dawkins said Wednesday that Kispert (thumb) will be ready for training camp, Chase Hughes of Monumental Sports Network reports. Kispert underwent successful surgery on his left thumb back on March 18, ending his 2024-25 campaign early. He finished the regular season with averages of 11.6 points, 3.0 rebounds, 2.0 three-pointers and 1.7 assists in 26.3 minutes per game. Presumably, he'll open the season as the primary backup small forward behind Khris Middleton.

Standing out in camp. Bucks head coach Doc Rivers said Tuesday that Anthony was "fantastic" to open training camp, according to Bucks Breakdown. Rivers also noted that Anthony "lived in the paint" for the entire opening practice. Milwaukee's head coach clearly likes what he's seen so far, and it seems like Anthony has the edge to win the backup point guard role behind Kevin Porter for the time being. Anthony saw his minutes get reduced in Orlando last season, but it's not unrealistic to think he can earn more than 20 minutes per game with his new team.

Goes through scrimmage Tuesday. Garland (toe) participated in a scrimmage with contact Tuesday, Chris Fedor of Cleveland.com reports. Garland is still on the mend after undergoing toe surgery in June. Although the Cavaliers have been encouraged by Garland's recent progress, head coach Kenny Atkinson cautioned that his return is not imminent. "It's not linear, usually, the return to performance, and we're hoping it will be and he'll progress," Atkinson said. "But I side on the side of being conservative and making sure. This is a good step today. A small step but a good step." The Cavaliers are likely to provide another update on Garland's timetable in the near future, but for now, fantasy managers can assume that he will miss a handful of games to open the regular season.

Goes through scrimmage Tuesday. Garland participated in a scrimmage with contact Tuesday, Chris Fedor of cleveland.com reports. Garland underwent surgery on his left great toe back in early June, and at the time, the Cavaliers announced a 4-to-5 month timetable. While Garland's participation Tuesday was a step in the right direction, coach Kenny Atkinson warned that his return is not imminent. "It was live. It was very short," Atkinson said of the scrimmage. Confident after healthy summer. Carter entered training camp feeling confident after enjoying a healthy summer, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports. Carter underwent a procedure two years ago that involved putting a plate in his left hand to stabilize a fracture, and he feels he hasn't logged a healthy summer since. That changed over the offseason, as Carter was able to rebuild some confidence and get his body ready for the upcoming 2025-26 season, rather than focusing on rehab work. "My confidence is at an all-time high right now," said Carter. "I'm feeling good. When I had this summer just to train, it wasn't necessarily about me becoming a better shooter -- I know I can shoot. It wasn't about me being able to make moves in the post like I know I can do. It was just about me boosting my confidence." Carter saw a decline in several key areas a year ago, as he averaged just 9.1 points on 46.0 percent shooting from the field and 23.4 percent from downtown in 68 regular-season matchups. A strong offseason could be just what he needs to get back on track.
